About us

Our story

Our work began in 2026 with the Network for Syrian Legislative Studies (NSLS), a volunteer initiative bringing together students and researchers from universities in Syria and abroad to support Syria’s new People’s Assembly. We began publishing policy proposals, engaging with lawmakers, and making parliamentary proceedings more accessible to the public.

As we build relationships in Damascus, new projects began to take shape. We joined with Syria Direct to establish Sada House, a cultural space in central Damascus. And we began forming chapters at US universities and launched policy clinics for university students in Syria so that more young Syrians could participate in policymaking.

These efforts grew organically, enabled by volunteers’ time and donated space. Our small network of volunteers became a broader initiative to open new avenues for political participation and public debate.

Syria Civic brings these activities together under one organization. Our Ideas Initiative develops policy proposals and works with legislators; Civic Futures supports young Syrians through university networks, fellowships, and civic initiatives; and Sada House brings people together across professions and generations for discussion and exchange.

We're building the institutions, networks, and spaces that can help more Syrians take part in shaping their country's future.
